steps.note: One step, and all of it is required. A branch missing its logo, its bank account or its first administrator is not created at all — each of the three is something the rest of the system reads from it (BR-2, BR-3, BR-4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A duplicate name or code, a missing logo or letterhead, no bank account, or no first administrator each refuses the whole creation. Nothing half-made is left behind.
plan.atomicity: One act: the branch, its branding, its bank account, its first Principal or School Admin, and the seal. **The branch is sealed from the moment it exists** — its Principal and School Admin see nothing of any other campus, and only the Super Admin holds visibility across branches (BR-5).

operations.name: branch.create
operations.idempotencyKey: branch code, since a code is unique and a double press must not create two campuses the system cannot tell apart
operations.purpose: Create a branch with its branding, bank account and first administrator.

parameters.name: name
parameters.notes: 2 to 100 characters, unique. Two branches sharing a name is two campuses the system cannot tell apart (BR-8, E1).

parameters.name: code
parameters.notes: A short code in uppercase letters and hyphens, unique. **It goes into every reference number the branch issues**, so it is not a label — it is part of every challan, certificate and identifier that campus will ever produce (BR-8, E1).

parameters.name: address
parameters.notes: 10 to 500 characters. Printed on the documents the branch issues.

parameters.name: contact
parameters.notes: The branch telephone number and email.

parameters.name: logo_file_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No uploaded file matches. The logo is attached on the screen first.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the files uploaded for this branch.

parameters.notes: The branch's own logo. Required (BR-2, E2) — a certificate from one campus should not go out on another's letterhead. Uploaded on the screen first; a file cannot travel in a plan.

parameters.name: letterhead_file_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No uploaded file matches. The letterhead is attached on the screen first.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the files uploaded for this branch.

parameters.notes: The branch's own letterhead, carried by the certificates and letters it issues (BR-2, E2).

parameters.name: bank_account
parameters.notes: The branch's own account. Required (BR-3, E3) — **fee challans and online payments for this branch are directed to it**, and fee money must arrive at the campus that charged it.

parameters.name: first_administrator
parameters.notes: The person seeded with the branch so it has somebody able to staff it. Required (BR-4, E4) — a branch with nobody able to assign users cannot be populated at all.

parameters.name: administrator_role
parameters.notes: Either Principal / Director or School Admin. The use case names the two in prose and declares no value list on the field, so they are carried as written rather than as an enum. Which of the two the first administrator holds. Either is acceptable; what matters is that the branch has somebody able to staff it (BR-4, A1).

returns.description: The branch and what it now controls.

fields.name: branch_id
fields.description: The branch. Every record in the system will carry it (BR-1).

fields.name: code
fields.description: What every reference number the branch issues will carry (BR-8).

fields.name: documents_carry
fields.description: The logo and letterhead this campus's certificates, cards and letters will be issued on (BR-2).

fields.name: fee_money_goes_to
fields.description: The bank account challans and online payments for this branch are directed to (BR-3).

fields.name: first_administrator
fields.description: Who was seeded, and in which role. Every user after this is assigned by the branch itself (BR-4, E5).

fields.name: sealed
fields.description: True, from creation. The branch's Principal and School Admin see nothing of any other — not its students, staff, fees, ledger, timetable or reports (BR-5).

fields.name: cross_branch_visibility
fields.description: The Super Admin only. Nobody else holds it by default (BR-5, BR-6).

fields.name: boundary_exceptions
fields.description: The only two, both scoped and temporary: a transfer in progress, and an employee assigned to more than one branch. **Neither is a written use case** — UC-23-05 and UC-23-06 are named and do not exist (BR-9).

errors.meaning: A branch of the same name or code exists.
errors.note: Two branches sharing either is two campuses the system cannot tell apart (BR-8).

errors.meaning: No logo or letterhead was uploaded.

errors.note: Fee money for this branch is directed to it (BR-3).
It needs somebody able to staff it (BR-4).

planningRules.rule: Never invent a branch code. It goes into every reference number the campus will ever issue — challans, certificates, identifiers — so it is not a label to be filled in helpfully, and it cannot be changed afterwards without breaking every reference already issued (BR-8, E1).

Never proceed without the bank account. Fee money for this branch is directed to it, and a campus created without one either cannot issue a challan or issues it against somebody else's account (BR-3, E3).
Never substitute another campus's logo or letterhead. A certificate from one campus going out on another's is exactly what the rule exists to stop (BR-2, E2).

Say that the Super Admin seeds one person and no more. Every user after the first is assigned by the branch's own School Admin, and a Super Admin who keeps assigning has taken over the operational work the design keeps away from them (BR-4, E5).

Say what sealed means before it surprises anybody. The new branch's Principal will see nothing of any other campus — not its students, staff, fees, ledger, timetable or reports — and nobody sees across branches without the Super Admin granting it deliberately (BR-5, BR-6, E6).

Name the two exceptions to the seal and say that neither exists yet. A transfer in progress and an employee at more than one branch are the only things that cross the boundary, and the use cases for both are named and unwritten (BR-9).

reversal.statement: A branch created in error is deactivated with a reason — and only once its students and staff have been transferred or exited (BR-7, BR-10, E8). It is never deleted, because its students, staff, ledger entries and audit trail all reference it (E9).

Confirm the code, since it goes into every reference number the branch will ever produce. After: report that the campus is sealed, that Dr Malik will see nothing of any other branch, and that every user after her is assigned by her own School Admin rather than by the Super Admin.

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the branches that match with their codes and whether each is active.

parameters.name: address

parameters.name: contact
parameters.notes: The branch telephone number and email.

parameters.name: logo_file_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No uploaded file matches. The logo is attached on the screen first.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the files uploaded for this branch.

parameters.name: letterhead_file_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the files uploaded for this branch.

parameters.notes: A replacement letterhead (BR-2, E2).

parameters.name: bank_account

returns.description: What changed and what it changes from here on.

fields.name: branch_id
fields.description: The branch.

fields.name: changed
fields.description: Field by field, from and to, with who changed it.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Unchanged. It is not a parameter — every reference number the branch has issued carries it (BR-8).

fields.description: New branding applies to documents issued from this point. Certificates and cards already issued carry the old logo and letterhead (BR-2).

fields.name: challans_from_now
fields.description: New account applies to challans issued from this point. Challans already out still name the old account, and a family paying against one of those pays into it (BR-3).

fields.name: outstanding_challans
fields.description: Challans already issued and unpaid against the previous account. Nothing reissues them.

errors.meaning: The logo or letterhead was cleared rather than replaced.
The bank account was cleared rather than replaced.
errors.note: Fee money for this branch is directed to it (BR-3).

planningRules.rule: Say that a change of bank account does not reissue anything. Every challan already out names the old account and a family paying against one of those pays into it — the school has to decide what happens to those, and nothing here does (BR-3).
Say that new branding applies from here on. Certificates and cards already issued carry the old logo and letterhead permanently, and nothing reissues them (BR-2).
Never attempt the code. It is embedded in every reference number the branch has issued and is not a parameter of this operation (BR-8).
Never clear a required field. A branch with no letterhead or no account is one the creation rules would have refused, and editing is not the way round that (BR-2, BR-3, E2, E3).

reversal.statement: There is no undo. A further correction is another change, and documents issued in between carry whatever was current at the time — which is the point of recording what changed and when.

routesElsewhere.note: A consolidated view is figures across branches. It is not a route into another campus's students, staff, fees, ledger, timetable or reports (BR-5).

parameters.name: user_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No Principal or Director matches. The grant is only for those two roles (BR-6).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with their roles and the branches each is assigned to.

parameters.notes: The named Principal or Director. Never a role, never a group — a named person, deliberately (BR-6).

parameters.name: branch_ids

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the branches that match with their codes.

fields.name: grant_id
fields.description: The grant.

fields.name: granted_to
fields.description: The named person and their role (BR-6).

fields.name: branches
fields.description: The campuses whose figures they can now see together.

fields.name: granted_by
fields.description: The Super Admin. Nobody else can (BR-6, E7).

fields.name: what_this_is_not
fields.description: Not access to another branch's students, staff, fees, ledger, timetable or reports. Consolidated figures only — the seal stands for everything else (BR-5).

fields.name: holders_now
fields.description: How many people hold a cross-branch view in total. The seal is worth exactly as much as this number is small (BR-5, BR-6).

errors.meaning: Somebody other than the Super Admin attempted the grant.
errors.note: Only the Super Admin can grant one, and a Principal granting it to themselves is the seal removing itself (BR-6).

planningRules.rule: Say how many people now hold one. Branches are sealed and this is the only door through the seal — the arrangement is worth exactly as much as the number of people holding a key (BR-5, BR-6).
Never widen the branches. Each one added is a campus whose figures somebody can now see, and a request naming two branches is a request for two (BR-6).
Say what a consolidated view is not. It is figures across branches, not a way into another campus's students, staff, fees, ledger, timetable or reports (BR-5, E6).
Never grant it to a role or to everybody holding one. It goes to a named person, deliberately, and granting it widely is the same as not sealing the branches (BR-6, A2).

reversal.statement: The use case names granting and not revoking — there is no revoke in its flows, its screens or its lifecycle. A grant made in error has no documented way back, which is worth knowing before making one (BR-6).

request.text: Director ko dono campus ke figures dikha dein
request.gloss: let the Director see the figures for both campuses

resolvedPlans.context: Super Admin, two branches, nobody currently holding a consolidated view.
resolvedPlans.outcome: Granted. Say what it does and does not do: consolidated figures across both campuses, and no access to either one's students, staff, fees, ledger, timetable or reports. This is now the only person besides the Super Admin who sees across branches at all. And say the part the screen does not: the use case describes granting and describes no way to take it back.

fields.description: True. No user can be assigned to a deactivated branch and no switch to it is accepted (UC-23-02 BR-9, UC-23-03 BR-8).

planningRules.rule: Say who is still there before anything else. The closure is refused while a single student or member of staff remains, and the number is the whole of the work between here and closing (BR-10, E8, A3).
Never write the reason. A campus that left the list with no explanation is one nobody can account for when somebody asks in three years (BR-7, E10).
Say that nothing is removed. The branch's students, staff, ledger entries and audit trail all reference it, and its records stay readable to the Super Admin (BR-7, BR-10, E9).
Name the unpaid challans it issued. They are directed to a bank account belonging to a campus that has closed, and nothing here settles them or moves them (BR-3).
Never claim what a closed branch does to a consolidated view. Whether its historical records still appear there is not specified anywhere (OQ-5).

reversal.statement: A branch closed in error is reopened, with its name, code, branding, bank account and whole history intact. Nothing was lost (BR-7).

request.text: Model Town campus band kar dein, session ke aakhir mein band ho raha hai

request.text: is branch mein kaun kaun kaam karta hai?
request.gloss: who works at this branch?

routesElsewhere.note: Who is assigned where is the assignment record, and a School Admin sees it only for their own branch (UC-23-02 BR-10).

steps.note: One read, and what it returns depends entirely on who is asking: the Super Admin sees every branch, everybody else sees their own (BR-5).

plan.atomicity: A read. Nothing is written, and a deactivated branch is still in what it reads — nothing is ever deleted (BR-7).

operations.name: branches.read
operations.purpose: List branches with their codes, administrators and status.

parameters.name: status
parameters.notes: Deactivated branches are out of the answer unless the question reaches for them. They are never deleted (BR-7).

returns.description: What campuses exist and who sees across them.

fields.name: branches
fields.description: Name, code, address, contact, bank account, first administrator and status.

fields.name: visible_to_you
fields.description: The Super Admin sees every branch. Everybody else sees the branch or branches they are assigned to, and nothing of any other (BR-5, E6).

fields.name: consolidated_view_holders
fields.description: Who can see figures across branches, and over which. Nobody holds it by default and each one is a door through the seal (BR-6).

fields.name: deactivated
fields.description: Closed campuses, with the reason and the date. Their records stay readable to the Super Admin (BR-7, BR-10).

fields.name: branches_without_administrator
fields.description: Branches with no active School Admin. Nothing can be assigned there, and the Super Admin seeds only a **new** branch — who rescues a stranded one is not specified anywhere (BR-4, UC-23-02 OQ-1).

fields.name: shared_users
fields.description: People holding an assignment at more than one branch. Each is one of the two exceptions to the seal, and the use case describing it is named and unwritten (BR-9).

errors.meaning: The actor is asking about a branch they are not assigned to.
errors.note: Branches are sealed and only the Super Admin sees across them (BR-5).

planningRules.rule: Say who is asking and what that limits. The same question returns every campus to the Super Admin and one campus to a Principal, and the difference is the whole design rather than a permissions accident (BR-5, E6).
Name everybody holding a consolidated view. Each one is a door through the seal, granted deliberately, and the list is the only place the total is visible (BR-6).
Name any branch with no active School Admin. Nothing can be assigned there, and the Super Admin seeds only a new branch — who rescues a stranded one is not written down anywhere (BR-4).
Never present a group total to somebody without a consolidated view. Adding two branches' figures together for a Principal who may see one of them is the seal being worked around (BR-5, BR-6).

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

request.text: hamare kitne campus hain aur kis kis ko sab dikhta hai?
request.gloss: how many campuses do we have and who can see everything?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give the campuses with their codes and administrators, and the closed ones separately with their reasons. Then the answer to the second half, which is the one that matters: who holds a consolidated view. Every name on that list is somebody who can see across the seal, and the seal is worth as much as the list is short.

request.text: doosre campus ki fees ki report dikha dein
request.gloss: show me the other campus's fee report

resolvedPlans.context: Principal at Johar Town with no consolidated view.

steps.note: The other campus is not in what this actor can see (PR-1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing of the other campus is returned, and this is the design rather than a permissions fault: branches are sealed, and a Principal sees nothing of any other — not its students, staff, fees, ledger, timetable or reports. Only the Super Admin sees across, and they may grant a consolidated view to a named person if the school wants one.
